title: Weight grading of representations of arbitrary diagonalizable group schemes
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $M$ a finitely generated additive abelian group. Let $k[M]$ have basis $e_m$ indexed by $m\in M$, multiplication $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$, and antipode $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. Put $D_k(M)=\operatorname{Spec}k[M]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sc-group-scheme]. Its character $\chi_m:D_k(M)\to\mathbf G_m$ is dual to $t\mapsto e_m$, with $\mathbf G_m$ as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and $\rho:D_k(M)\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ a homomorphism of group schemes. Here $\operatorname{GL}(V)(A)=\operatorname{Aut}_A(V\otimes_k A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, with tensor products as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; in a basis this is [def-sc-general-linear-group], and for $V=0$ it is the trivial group. Define
$$V_m=\{v\in V:\rho_A(c)(v\otimes1)=v\otimes\chi_m(c)\text{ for every commutative }k\text{-algebra }A\text{ and }c\in D_k(M)(A)\}.$$
Only finitely many $V_m$ are nonzero, and the sum map $\bigoplus_{m\in M}V_m\to V$ is an isomorphism of vector spaces. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, the direct sum decomposition base changes to $V\otimes_k A=\bigoplus_m(V_m\otimes_k A)$, and $D_k(M)_A$ acts on $V_m\otimes_k A$ by $\chi_m$. Moreover, if an $A$-linear endomorphism $u$ of $V\otimes_k A$ commutes with the action of $D_k(M)(B)$ after extension to every commutative $A$-algebra $B$, then $u$ preserves every summand $V_m\otimes_k A$. All assertions allow $M=0$, $V=0$, and torsion in $M$, including torsion divisible by the characteristic of $k$.

source.place: Theorem 12.12(a) implies (d), and Remark 12.13, printed pp.234–235; coefficient projection proof gives the base-change decomposition and preservation by equivariant endomorphisms.

proof.text: Put $C=k[M]$. Choose finitely many group generators $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ of $M$. The elements $e_{a_i},e_{-a_i}$ generate $C$ as a $k$-algebra: every $m$ is an integral combination of the $a_i$, and the corresponding product is $e_m$. Thus $D_k(M)=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is affine of finite type (the single affine chart over the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ meets [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Apply [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] to $\rho$. It supplies a linear map $c:V\to V\otimes_k C$ with $(c\otimes1)c=(1\otimes\Delta)c$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)c=1$. If $c(v)=\sum_i v_i\otimes h_i$, then $\rho_A(x)(v\otimes a)=\sum_i v_i\otimes x(h_i)a$ for every $k$-algebra $A$ and $x:C\to A$. In particular $c(v)=\rho_C(\mathrm{id}_C)(v\otimes1)$. The dictionary allows $V=0$.

source.place: Remark 4.1, printed p.84, equations (24)--(25); Theorem 12.12(a) implies (b), printed p.235.

proof.text: For $h\in C$ write $[h]_m$ for its coefficient at $e_m$. For any $k$-vector space $W$, the bilinear formula $(w,h)\mapsto[h]_m w$ induces $E_m^W:W\otimes_k C\to W$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Expanding a finite sum of pure tensors gives $z=\sum_m E_m^W(z)\otimes e_m$, with finite support; applying $E_n^W$ shows uniqueness. Set $p_m=E_m^V c$, so $c(v)=\sum_m p_m(v)\otimes e_m$. All $p_m$ are linear. Tensor reassociation and unit identifications here are the maps on pure tensors $(v\otimes h)\otimes h'\leftrightarrow v\otimes(h\otimes h')$ and $v\otimes a\leftrightarrow av$; the inverse identities hold on the generating pure tensors.

source.place: Theorem 12.12(a) implies (b), printed p.235: expansion in the group-like basis; coefficient maps made explicit.

proof.text: The two coaction identities from Step 1, using the Hopf formulas in the statement, read $\sum_m c(p_m(v))\otimes e_m=\sum_m p_m(v)\otimes e_m\otimes e_m$ and $v=\sum_m p_m(v)$. Apply $E_n^{V\otimes C}$ from Step 2 to the last tensor factor in the first equality: $c(p_n(v))=p_n(v)\otimes e_n$. Consequently $p_m p_n=0$ for $m\ne n$ and $p_n^2=p_n$, by extracting the remaining coefficient $m$. These are finite identities for each vector; no infinite sum of operators is used.

source.place: Theorem 12.12(a) implies (b), printed p.235: coassociativity, counit and coefficient comparison.

proof.text: The equation $c(v)=v\otimes e_m$ is equivalent to $v\in V_m$. Forward: the formula of [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] gives $\rho_A(x)(v\otimes1)=v\otimes x(e_m)=v\otimes\chi_m(x)$ for every $A,x$. Reverse: use $A=C$ and the universal point $x=\mathrm{id}_C$; the same dictionary gives $c(v)=\rho_C(x)(v\otimes1)$, while $\chi_m(x)=e_m$ by the specified dual character map. Thus $V_m$ is the subspace cut out by a linear equation, $p_m(V)=V_m$, and $p_n|_{V_m}=\delta_{nm}\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Remark 4.1, printed p.84, universal element; Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, printed p.235.

proof.text: The sum map from the finite-support families defining [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] has inverse $v\mapsto(p_m(v))_m$: Step 3 gives the sum identity, and Step 4 recovers every component of a family. This proves the claimed isomorphism. Take a finite spanning list $v_1,\ldots,v_t$ of $V$ using [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and let $F$ be the union of their finite coefficient supports. For $m\notin F$, linearity implies $p_m=0$ on $V$; since it is the identity on $V_m$, that space is zero. Thus only finitely many summands are nonzero, including when the spanning list is empty.

source.place: Theorem 12.12(d) and Remark 12.13, printed pp.234--235; finite support from a finite spanning list.

proof.text: Write $j_m:V_m\hookrightarrow V$ and $q_m:V\to V_m$, $q_m(v)=p_m(v)$. Tensor the maps using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For each $A$, the sum map $J_A:\bigoplus_m(V_m\otimes_k A)\to V\otimes_k A$ induced by $j_m\otimes1$ has inverse $Q_A(v\otimes a)=(q_m(v)\otimes a)_m$. The latter exists by bilinearity and the tensor universal property; its values have support in the fixed finite set $F$ of Step 5. On generating pure tensors, $J_AQ_A(v\otimes a)=\sum_m p_m(v)\otimes a=v\otimes a$ and the $n$-component of $Q_AJ_A(w\otimes a)$ from the $m$-summand is $\delta_{nm}w\otimes a$. Hence both composites are identities, with no flatness hypothesis on $A$. In particular the summand maps are injective. Denote the corresponding projections on $V\otimes_k A$ by $P_m=p_m\otimes1$.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 coefficient projection argument, printed p.235; explicit tensor extension of the inverse sum map.

proof.text: For $w\in V_m$, Step 4 and the all-algebras formula of [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] give $\rho_A(x)(w\otimes a)=w\otimes\chi_m(x)a$. Pure tensors generate $V_m\otimes_k A$, so this is scalar action on the entire summand. The same computation for every $A$-algebra $B$ proves that the base-changed group scheme $D_k(M)_A$ acts by the base-changed character, rather than merely giving a formula on its $A$-points.

source.place: Definition 12.11 and Theorem 12.12, printed pp.234--235, all-algebras action; Remark 12.13.

proof.text: Fix $A$ and $u$ as in the statement. Use the commutative $A$-algebra $B=A[M]$, the finite formal sums $\sum_m a_me_m$ with $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$. Let $x\in D_k(M)(B)$ be the point $C\to B$, $e_m\mapsto e_m$. Put $W=V\otimes_k A$. Under the canonical identification $(V\otimes_k A)\otimes_A B\simeq V\otimes_k B$, $((v\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto v\otimes ab$ with inverse $v\otimes b\mapsto(v\otimes1)\otimes b$, Step 7 gives $\rho_B(x)(z\otimes1)=\sum_m P_m(z)\otimes e_m$ for every $z\in W$. Commutation with $u_B=u\otimes1$ therefore gives $\sum_m P_m(u z)\otimes e_m=\sum_m u(P_m z)\otimes e_m$. Extract the coefficient $n$ via the $A$-bilinear map $(w,\sum_m a_me_m)\mapsto a_nw$, whose induced tensor map exists by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. It follows that $P_nu=uP_n$. If $z$ belongs to the $n$-summand, $P_nz=z$, whence $P_nu(z)=u(z)$; its image is the same summand by Step 6. Thus $u$ preserves every summand.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, printed p.235, coefficient method; preservation follows by the displayed universal-point calculation.

proof.text: When $M=0$, $C=k$ and the counit says $c(v)=v\otimes1$; the only weight is $0$ with $V_0=V$. When $V=0$, all summands and maps are zero and the decomposition is the empty sum. The zero test algebra also gives the zero module. For torsion $M$, the $e_m$ remain distinct formal basis vectors even if $k[M]$ is nonreduced: for example, in characteristic $p$, $k[\mathbf Z/p]=k[t]/(t^p-1)$ still has basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{p-1}$. Every coefficient calculation above uses this formal basis and no division by a group order, smoothness, reducedness, or separation by $k$-points. Thus all stated torsion and characteristic cases are included.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, printed pp.234--235, arbitrary diagonalizable groups; edge cases written out.

proof_origin.place: Remark 4.1, printed p.84; Theorem 12.12(a) implies (d), and Remark 12.13, printed pp.234--235. Explicit coefficient calculations also prove the stated scalar-extension and equivariant-endomorphism consequences.
